Related work establishes the ingredients, but this search did not identify the exact five-item formula. [MAN (WSDM 2024)](https://fi.ee.tsinghua.edu.cn/~gaochen/papers/WSDM2024-MAN.pdf) combines sequential backbones including SASRec with similarity-weighted historical-item representations, in a cross-domain setting. [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) introduced zero-initialized scalar residual gates; [nanoSASRec](https://github.com/eifuentes/nanoSASRec) explicitly implements ReZero with SASRec. Thus similarity pooling and zero-initialized residuals have clear precedents; the particular combination warrants evaluation, without claiming a fundamentally new mechanism.

Analytically, for nonzero embeddings and lag k=t−j, the latest logit is 1, while an older logit is −k+cₖ, where cₖ≤1. Therefore wₜ₋ₖ/wₜ=exp(−k+cₖ−1)≤exp(−k): no older item can outweigh the latest. With five valid inputs, wₜ≥1/(1+e⁻¹+e⁻²+e⁻³+e⁻⁴)=0.636. If older cosine similarities are zero, wₜ≈0.826. Self-similarity therefore makes pooling at least as latest-heavy as decay alone; dissimilar older items strengthen that bias. This measures agreement with the latest embedding, not independent evidence of repeated interest.

Retrain matched variants: plain SASRec; identical gated branch using only eₜ; decay-only pooling, softmax(−k); full pooling; and leave-self-out pooling over the same four earlier positions, both with and without cosine weighting. Keep normalization, gate, optimization, seeds, and validation candidates fixed. Compare macro validation HR@10 and per-category gains; measure self-weight, gate magnitude, and effects across earlier-history similarity levels. Full pooling beating latest-only and decay-only, plus cosine improving leave-self-out pooling, supports useful historical agreement. Similar performance across controls suggests a recency shortcut. Similarity-shuffled weights provide an additional control.
